title: Ledger and Witness
premise: Mirabel Pemberton, a retired detective whose quiet bookshop life is a deliberate act of forgetting, is pulled back into investigation when a drowned man washes up wearing clothes cut from Mirabel's own wardrobe—clothes only one person could have taken: the witness Mirabel buried in memory and official records alike. The victim, it emerges, was hired to find that same 'dead' witness, whose testimony once convicted an innocent man on the eve of an anniversary dinner that still celebrates the case. As the dinner approaches, Mirabel must choose between protecting their own hidden complicity and exposing the truth, confronting the witness—who is alive, watching, and has been leaving the clothes as messages. In the end, Mirabel publicly recants the old testimony at the anniversary toast, trading reputation for justice, while the witness finally steps out of the shadows to forgive—or not.
about_author: Tamsin Joubert spent fifteen years as a court archivist in Cape Town before turning to fiction, a career that left her fluent in the gap between what is recorded and what is true. She writes mysteries about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Coat
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A body in the canal wears Mirabel's missing grey overcoat, and the police—knowing Mirabel's past—treat her as suspect rather than colleague. Searching the shop, she finds a pressed violet, the flower from a case twenty years ago. The emotional beat: dread sharpening into recognition; the past has found her address.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She Drowned
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with flashbacks. She reopens the old file: the witness, Ada Voss, officially dead, whose testimony Mirabel coached and quietly doubted. The victim turns out to be a genealogist hired by the anniversary committee to verify Ada's death. Beat: guilt curdling as Mirabel realizes someone else was asking the same questions—and died for it.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, racing the clock. Following the violets and coat clues, she finds Ada living under another name; Ada reveals the clothes were messages, testing whether Mirabel would finally look. But the committee's chairman, the true architect of the false conviction, learns Ada lives. Beat: terror and tenderness entwined—Mirabel must protect the woman she wronged by morning.

chapters.title: Raise the Glass
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV at the anniversary dinner. Confronting the chairman among the toasts, she lays out his forgery of Ada's statement, then publicly recants her own role in coaching it. Ada enters unannounced; the room fractures; the chairman is taken. Final beat: outside, Ada offers Mirabel neither absolution nor blame—only her hand, and a beginning.
